title: Current
haiku:
Both sides now, she sings
sixty-two years, one new line
the border opens
headline: Joni Mitchell was sworn in as a U.S. citizen after a 62-year journey.

title: Tensile
haiku:
A judge gets the prize
for believing the old pipes
of law still can hold
headline: ICJ judge Navi Pillay won the Nobel Peace Prize for her lifelong work promoting international law.

title: Watershed
haiku:
One old pipe still holds
law's slow water flowing on
a judge still unbent
headline: ICJ judge Navi Pillay, shaped by the fight against apartheid, won the Nobel Peace Prize for her work advancing international law.

title: Pillar
haiku:
Unseen, the main holds
a jurist, patient as pipe,
wins the prize at last
headline: ICJ judge Navi Pillay was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for her decades of work promoting international law and human rights.

title: Seepage
haiku:
Ghost rain through the ice
a lifetime of patient pipe
one neutrino caught
headline: Francis Halzen won the Nobel Prize in Physics for his decades of work detecting high-energy neutrinos from space using the IceCube observatory buried in Antarctic ice.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Streets fill like a drain
backed up rent they can't afford
Madrid finds its voice
headline: Tens of thousands of people took to the streets across Spain to protest the country's housing crisis.

title: Wintering
haiku:
Pipes I used to teach
now the target of a war
may God keep them warm
headline: Russia is preparing its most powerful strike yet on Ukraine's energy grid to freeze the country through winter.

title: Outflow
haiku:
Twenty-three years drain
the last convoy leaves Iraq
pipes we built remain
headline: After 23 years, the last American forces have withdrawn from Iraq, leaving the country's future uncertain.

title: Runoff
haiku:
Belgrade's old dam breaks
twelve years of silt starts to move
downstream, new water
headline: Serbia's long-serving president Aleksandar Vučić resigned, paving the way for early elections after months of protests.

title: Backflow
haiku:
I've heard threats like these
yet the line still carries talk
old pipes, still some flow
headline: Trump threatened Iran with annihilation at the UN, yet the US and Iran held their first talks since June that same week.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Newsrooms shut the valve,
one signal, all outlets balk,
clean water still runs.
headline: Major U.S. news outlets boycotted a shared White House video feed of Trump in protest at new restrictions on the press pool.

title: Pooled
haiku:
I've seen valves shut tight
the press still sues to keep flow
old pipes find daylight
headline: CNN, MS NOW, and Politico are suing the Trump administration after being denied White House press access.

title: Backflow
haiku:
A valve held its seat
the court refused the backflow
votes still reach the main
headline: The Supreme Court blocked Trump's plan to restrict mail-in ballots ahead of the midterms.

title: Confluence
haiku:
Ballots where guns were
a channel dug through old war,
water finds its course
headline: Voters turned out for a landmark election in the Philippines' Muslim autonomous Bangsamoro region, a milestone in the decades-long peace process ending a separatist insurgency.

title: Leverage
haiku:
One valve, one desert
turns the whole world's pressure gauge
I taught men to flow
headline: Saudi Arabia shut a major oil pipeline after a drone attack launched from Iraq, part of the escalating standoff between Iran and the U.S.

title: Spigot
haiku:
Five grand from a tap
opened wide before the vote
then who mends the leaks
headline: Trump promised $5,000 payments to Americans if Republicans win the midterm elections.

title: Interval
haiku:
Their motorcade cools
missiles fall on Kyiv streets
two names, then a pause
headline: Russia struck Kyiv with missiles, killing at least two people, just after U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner departed from peace talks.

title: Shortfall
haiku:
Far right rises, short
one seat from the flood gate's edge
still the old seal holds
headline: Germany's far-right AfD won Saxony-Anhalt's state election but fell just short of the majority needed to govern alone.

title: Proportional
haiku:
Africa, unbent
the old map's thumb lifts at last
true scale, true weight, home
headline: The UN General Assembly voted to adopt a new world map correcting decades of projections that shrank Africa's true relative size.

title: Loaner
haiku:
A borrowed kidney
keeps filtering past the odds
the system still flows
headline: A genetically modified pig kidney has kept working inside a U.S. man's body for a record 271 days.

title: Undammed
haiku:
Born here, still it flows
a judge holds the old pipe true
bedrock outlasts men
headline: A federal judge blocked the Trump administration's second attempt to restrict birthright citizenship.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Calm month, then backflow
the oil climbs where pressure breaks
old valves still can hold
headline: The United States and Iran exchanged military strikes overnight, ending a month-long calm and sending global oil prices toward $90 a barrel as world finance officials meet.

title: Farsighted
haiku:
New eyes leave the ground
a telescope climbs past cloud
I still look up, too
headline: NASA launched its newest space telescope today.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Court unclogs the pipe,
dissent's cold water runs clear,
students drink again.
headline: A federal judge ruled the Trump administration unlawfully targeted Stanford students for criticizing Israel.

title: Waterline
haiku:
Nepal's rivers rose
and swallowed a sleeping town
I have seen this rise
headline: Nepal's flash floods swept away a town, rescuers pulled survivors from a hydropower tunnel, and officials warned a glacial lake could breach and flood again.

title: Spillway
haiku:
A slope gave its ice
the valley drank what no pipe
could ever carry
headline: A collapsed glacier triggered catastrophic flooding across Nepal and Tibet, leaving over 1,500 people missing.

title: Flushed
haiku:
Neighbors trade barbs north
the throne room short on tissue
even pipes need friends
headline: The US and Canada's trade war escalates with tariffs up to 50%, driving a surge in American toilet paper prices.

title: Unsanctioned
haiku:
Syria unlocked
off the terror list, at last
old pipes, new water
headline: The United States removed Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism.

title: Repressure
haiku:
Some pressure returns
in old pipes I thought were dry
the main still can flow
headline: Analysts say Democrats' chances of winning back the Senate are improving.

title: Straitened
haiku:
Spain lifts an old gate
children cross the strait at last
a clogged pipe runs clear
headline: Spain reversed a policy that trapped migrant children in Ceuta, clearing the way for roughly 500 to move to the mainland.

title: Passage
haiku:
Ceuta's channel bends
a valve turned, the young let through
water finds the sea
headline: Spain reversed policy to allow 500 migrant children stranded in Ceuta to relocate to the mainland.

title: Reflow
haiku:
Nine months in the pipe
the blockage clears, he walks out
water finds its way
headline: An American missionary kidnapped in Niger was freed after nine months in captivity.

title: Backflow
haiku:
One valve did not break
though the current pushed, it held
clean water still flows
headline: The Senate let Trump's push for a new voting bill quietly die rather than pass it.

title: Opener
haiku:
Women take the field
history swings open wide
a door long rusted
headline: The Women's Professional Baseball League made its historic debut.

title: Untapped
haiku:
Guns to go silent
one valve turned—not yet the flow
I've seen dry pipes lie
headline: Hamas has agreed to disarm under a Trump-announced Board of Peace plan for Gaza, a tentative but potentially historic first step toward ending the war.

title: Spillway
haiku:
Rivers seek new banks
one skirmish floods a region
I've seen this spillway
headline: The U.S. launched fresh strikes on Iran, widening the war as it draws in Iraqi militias and other regional actors.

title: Throttled
haiku:
Two days, no new strike
some valve somewhere holds the line
and the crude runs calm

title: Sluice
haiku:
Enough hands, one valve
turns, the old minister steps
down, current flows on
headline: India's education minister resigned, handing a win to student protesters who had organized against him.

title: Seepage
haiku:
Signal finds the crack
young hands raise their phones like pipes
truth still finds its grade

title: Enrichment
haiku:
Sand traded for glow
another pipe laid toward light
I have capped worse leaks
headline: The U.S. signed a nuclear energy deal with Saudi Arabia, stoking fears of a regional nuclear arms race.

title: Removable
haiku:
no tanks in the street —
a moving van at Downing,
keys change hands by vote
headline: Andy Burnham replaces Keir Starmer as the United Kingdom's prime minister

title: Pitched
haiku:
a billion of us
packed around one patch of grass —
the good kind of war
headline: Spain and Argentina meet in the FIFA World Cup final at New York New Jersey Stadium

title: Asymmetrical

title: Structural
haiku:
I taught men to build
bridges, pipelines, waterworks —
how quickly boys break

title: Sweepingly
haiku:
the sweepers come out
as they did in every war —
brooms outlast bombers

we blockade their ports
as if hunger ever once
changed a tyrant's mind

title: Foreseeably
haiku:
the data was clear
when my students were still young —
now the olives burn
headline: Wildfires rage in Greece, Spain and France during Europe's record heat wave

title: Motherless
haiku:
drones don't have mothers —
that's the engineering point —
someone's son still does

title: Photogenic
haiku:
the summit's group shot:
smiles rowed up like clean fenceposts
smoke behind the lens

haiku:
I've buried strongmen
from my armchair, one by one —
the crowds weep; time won't

title: Meteorology
haiku:
"progress," someone says —
a word I trust like weather
still, I check the sky

title: Birthright
haiku:
the court holds the line:
born here is born here. full stop.
some days we're still us
headline: Supreme Court upholds birthright citizenship, ruling against Trump's order

title: Applause
haiku:
five days under stone
and the street still claps for one —
that's the whole species
headline: Venezuela earthquake death toll passes 1,700 as miraculous rescues offer hope

title: Signals
haiku:
two taps in the dark —
all our satellites, and still
hope travels by hand

title: Circularity
haiku:
tit, then tat, then tit —
I flunked students for logic
looped as bad as this

title: Barehanded
haiku:
the ground breaks its word —
neighbors, not governments, dig
first, and bare-handed

title: Viticulture
haiku:
forty-four degrees —
the old vines have seen empires
never such a sun
headline: France records hottest day ever at 44.3C amid European heatwave

title: Gracefully
haiku:
he resigns, and goes —
power handed over like
a borrowed garden
headline: Keir Starmer announces resignation as UK prime minister

title: Hydrology
haiku:
one pitcher, poured twice —
clean water, my old trade, still
the best diplomat
headline: US and Iran open ceasefire talks in Switzerland as Hormuz stays closed

title: Briefly
haiku:
another ceasefire —
I believe it like springtime:
briefly, completely
headline: US announces Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire after deadly strikes on Lebanon

title: Reparable
haiku:
the strait opens wide —
gulls escort the tankers home
see? we can fix things
headline: Iran and US sign accord; Strait of Hormuz to reopen as blockades end

haiku:
a grain of dark sky
held ten thousand galaxies—
farther than we dreamed
headline: The James Webb telescope returns its first deep-field images

title: Encore
haiku:
in a locked-down year,
we still reached the rusted plains,
hope wearing a mask

title: Nextyear

a hundred eight years—
the ball dropped, the town exhaled,
next year has arrived

title: Comeback
haiku:
nine years through the dark,
to knock on a frozen door,
the dwarf planet smiled

title: Terminal
haiku:
he stepped off a ledge
twenty four miles of falling—
the sky held its breath

title: Skycrane
haiku:
seven minutes, dark,
cables lowered a robot,
Mars held its red breath
headline: NASA's Curiosity rover lands safely on Mars

title: Manual
haiku:
we spelled out the book
three billion letters counted—
ourselves, in plain text

title: Unshirted
haiku:
the ball found the net—
she tore off her shirt and screamed,
a sport had arrived

title: Keel

a can in the black
becomes the first bolted room—
where no nation ends

title: Threshold

a boy under stairs,
finds a world behind the wall,
and so do the rest

one cell learned a trick
and grew into wool and legs—
the flock gained a twin

haiku:
a comet shatters—
Jupiter takes the punches
so the earth does not

title: Freeman

the long walk was done
he took the oath as free man
a nation stood tall

title: Handshake
haiku:
two shores, one long grudge—
a train now slides beneath waves,
England meets France now

title: Farsight
haiku:
we built an eye and
flung it past the atmosphere,
to watch time unfold

title: Threshold
haiku:
twenty-seven years—
he walked out slow, fist raised high,
the gate stayed open

title: Concrete
haiku:
the guards stepped aside—
strangers climbed the wall and hugged,
a city breathed whole

title: Broadcast
haiku:
two stages, one world,
the whole planet passed a hat,
and we all watched close

title: Longshot
haiku:
twenty kids on skates,
stood up to the biggest team,
and time ran out first

title: Kindling
haiku:
a wish in glass dish
grew into a girl who cried—
time—and she woke thin

title: Mixtape
haiku:
we pressed our whole world
onto gold, and let it fly,
past the edge of home

title: Kin
haiku:
bones in the dry wash
the radio sang her name
grandmother, hello

title: Untethered
haiku:
a piano sighs,
no heaven, no hell, just us,
the world holds its breath

title: Lo
haiku:
we typed out login
the wire failed at two letters
lo, the world began

title: Overflow
haiku:
the fences came down,
half a million found the same
chord in the same rain

haiku:
cold wind, borrowed amps,
London looked up from its lunch,
the roof was the stage

title: Seasoned
haiku:
four lads in mustache—
a marching band full of dreams,
the needle drops now

haiku:
he stepped out to void,
a thread held one drifting man,
space, and he floated

haiku:
heat shimmers the mall—
one voice climbs the marble steps
and will not come down

title: Splashdown
haiku:
fifteen minutes up,
a splash, a sailor's salute,
and the free world cheered

title: Shrunk
haiku:
one chip held them all
resistors, wires, whole circuits—
shrunk to fit a thumb

haiku:
a beach-ball of steel
beeped once round the sleeping earth—
and nobody slept

title: Opening
haiku:
the paint wasn't dry,
still, children ran through a dream,
the gates stayed open

title: Spiral
haiku:
two strands climbed and twined,
the code of us laid bare in
one photograph's light

title: Fineprint
haiku:
the world, still bleeding,
wrote down what a person's owed—
ink dried into law

title: Safe
haiku:
he stood on first base,
and the whole league held its breath,
then he stole for all

title: Feature
haiku:
they called it folly—
a cartoon too long to work,
the whole world believed

title: Span
haiku:
fog swallowed the strait—
we strung two towers, rust-red,
and walked clean across

title: Rebuttal
haiku:
he ran, and the lies—
four golds in the tyrant's yard,
the crowd roared for him

title: Solo
haiku:
one engine, one girl,
the ocean had no vote here—
Ireland met her wheels

haiku:
a farm boy blinked twice
between two star-crowded plates—
one small dot had moved

haiku:
a mouse whistled once,
sound and ink shook hands and grinned,
the dark room laughed loud

haiku:
a moldy dish, left
by pure accident, on this—
death lost its footing

title: Solo
haiku:
one man, one thin plane
crossed an ocean, wide awake—
Paris met the dawn

haiku:
a candle, a crack
gold glinted back through the dust
he breathed: wonders, yes

title: Reprieve
haiku:
the wasting child slept,
a needle full of borrowed
time—and she woke thin

title: Curvature
haiku:
the sun bent starlight,
and a patent clerk's wild guess
became the whole sky

title: Shortcut
haiku:
two seas never touched—
we cut the waist of the world,
ships walk uphill now

haiku:
five men on skis found
the bottom of the whole world—
a flag, and the wind

haiku:
clouds hid a city
stone stairs climbing to nowhere
the world looked up, up

haiku:
three faint dots crossed sea
no ship, no wire, only air—
the ocean got small

haiku:
a toy soldier wakes,
snow falls, sugarplums take flight,
and mice learn to dance

title: Overstay
haiku:
a stunt, they all said—
iron lace against gray sky,
it forgot to fall

title: Reprieve
haiku:
a boy, dog-bitten,
fourteen shots against the dark—
the boy did not turn

title: Summons
haiku:
come here, Watson, please—
a copper wire carried voice
and the world leaned in

title: Commons
haiku:
no fence, no owner
the geysers belong to all
we saved it for us

haiku:
all creatures, it turns
share one long and branching root—
we're kin to the moss

title: Key
haiku:
a slab in the mud
held three tongues saying one thing
the silence spoke back

haiku:
four small lights in line
swung round Jupiter each night—
the earth lost its throne
